```{r}
library(tidyverse)  # dplyr, ggplot2, lubridate, readr, stringr, tidyr ...
```

# I/ Get Data

## A) Diverse Financial Databases using Tidy Finance Shortcut

### 1) Fama-French database

FF3 model is used to **calculate the normal (expected)** return in event studies based on the Market premium, the Size premium and the Book-to-Market premium.

1)  Rm-rf is the market's excess return (compensation for overall market risk)
2)  SMB (**Small Minus Big**) is the return spread between **small-cap and large-cap** **portfolios** capturing the size premium **(small firms have historically earned higher average returns)**
3)  HML (**High Minus Low**) is the return spread between **high and low book-to-market portfolios** capturing the value premium **(value stocks (high BtM) outperforming growth stocks)**

Each row is a **month**, and each factor column (`mkt_excess`, `smb`, `hml`) is that month's **realized premium (**that month's value-weighted market return minus the risk-free rate, that month's small-portfolio return minus big-portfolio return (the realized size premium that month, that month's high-BM-portfolio return minus low-BM-portfolio return (the realized value premium that month).

So a value like `smb = 0.0213` means small stocks beat big stocks by **2.13% that particular month**

![](images/clipboard-758572383.png)

**FF3 (and CAPM) have 3 main roles:**

**Role 1 — Benchmark for abnormal returns (event studies, your CAR pipeline):**\

FF3 generates the expected return; you subtract it from the realized return; the residual (AR) is your object of interest, attributed to the *event*. Here FF3's output feeds a **subtraction**.

**Role 2 — Controls alongside a new variable (regressions):**\

FF3 betas/factors sit on the right-hand side next to your candidate variable (key-man score, or in Fama-MacBeth: size, bm). The factors absorb known effects so the coefficient on *your* variable is clean. Here FF3's terms are **competing regressors**.

And there's a **third classic role** worth adding to complete the picture:

**Role 3 — The model itself as the thing being tested:**\

Run FF3 on a portfolio or fund and look at **alpha**. If a fund manager claims skill, or someone claims a new anomaly, α ≠ 0 after FF3 says "there's return the model can't explain"; α = 0 says "your 'skill' was just size/value/market exposure." This is FF3 as judge rather than servant — performance evaluation and anomaly testing.

It expends on the CAPM theory which lacks of the ability to explain several empirically documented return patterns using market risk (beta) alone.

Using [Prof.Kenneth French’s finance data library](https://mba.tuck.dartmouth.edu/pages/faculty/ken.french/data_library.html) and TidyFinance shortcut:

```{r}
factors_ff3_monthly <- download_data(
  domain = "famafrench",
  dataset = "Fama/French 3 Factors",
  start_date = start_date,
  end_date = end_date
)
```

```{r}
write_parquet(factors_ff3_monthly, "data-r/factors_ff3_monthly.parquet")
```

All Fama-French datasets available from :

```{r}
list_supported_datasets(domain = "Fama-French")
```

### 2) Q-Factor database

The **q-factor model** (Hou, Xue, and Zhang, 2015 and 2021 for fifth factor extension) is an alternative 5-factor **asset pricing model** grounded in **investment-based (q-theory) economics** rather than the Fama-French empirical/characteristics approach.

1)  Rm-rf is the market's excess return (compensation for overall market risk)
2)  ME (Size factor) is analogous to SMB; return spread between small and big firms
3)  I/A (Investment factor) is the return spread between low-investment and high-investment firms (firms with low asset growth outperform firms with high asset growth)
4)  ROE (Profitability factor) is the return spread between high and low return-on-equity (ROE) firms
5)  EG (expected growth), this is the 5th factor from the **q⁵ model** (Hou, Xue, Zhang, extended 2021), which adds expected investment growth on top of the original q-factor model to better capture value-like patterns

![](images/clipboard-942974780.png)

Q-Factor <https://global-q.org/background.html>

```{r}
factors_q <- download_data(
  domain = "Global Q",
  dataset = "q5_factors_monthly_2024",
  start_date = start_date,
  end_date = end_date
)
```

```{r}
write_parquet(factors_q, "data-r/factors_q.parquet")
```

All Global Q dataset available:

```{r}
list_supported_datasets(domain = "Global Q")
```

### 3) Amit Goyal database (macroeconomic predictors)

A set of macroeconomic and financial variables commonly used to predict the **equity risk premium** (i.e., forecast future stock market excess returns), hosted publicly on Amit Goyal's website and updated periodically.

rp_div — Equity risk premium (market return minus risk-free rate) ; the variable being predicted

dp — Dividend-price ratio (log): log(dividends) - log(price)

dy — Dividend yield (log): log(dividends) - log(lagged price)

ep — Earnings-price ratio (log): log(earnings) - log(price)

de — Dividend-payout ratio (log): log(dividends) - log(earnings)

svar — Stock variance: sum of squared daily market returns within the month

bm — Book-to-market ratio for the aggregate market (DJIA book value / market value)

ntis — Net equity expansion: 12-month moving sum of net equity issuance by NYSE stocks / total market

cap tbl — Treasury bill rate (3-month T-bill secondary market rate)

lty — Long-term government bond

yield ltr — Long-term government bond return

tms — Term spread = lty - tbl

dfy — Default yield spread = BAA corporate bond yield - AAA corporate bond yield

infl — Inflation rate (CPI, all urban consumers), typically lagged one month

![](images/clipboard-861685376.png)

```{r}
macro_predictors <- download_data(
  domain = "Goyal-Welch", # or macro_predictors
  dataset = "monthly",
  start_date = start_date,
  end_date = end_date
)
```

```{r}
write_parquet(macro_predictors, "data-r/macro_predictors.parquet")
```

All macro predictors

```{r}
list_supported_datasets(domain = "Goyal-Welch")
```

But only until 2022. For more recent data, check on <https://sites.google.com/view/agoyal145> under [A Comprehensive 2022 Look at the Empirical Performance of Equity Premium Prediction](https://drive.google.com/file/d/11HdJIDvZtlhrZLTwHgVq1ocmhMpa_eTN/view?usp=sharing) in "Main publications" and download manually.

## B) WRDS

```{r}
wrds <- dbConnect(
  Postgres(),
  host = "wrds-pgdata.wharton.upenn.edu",
  dbname = "wrds",
  port = 9737,
  sslmode = "require",
  user = Sys.getenv("WRDS_USER"),
  password = Sys.getenv("WRDS_PASSWORD")
)

# Don't forget to add a .Renviron file to store credentials locally only.
```

### 1) CRSP

- Create **two lazy reference tables**

```{r}
# We need two tables

# (i) CRSP monthly security file (price, column, return etc...) 

msf_db <- tbl(wrds, I("crsp.msf_v2")) 

# (ii) the identifying information (sharetype, exchange, trading status etc...)

stksecurityinfohist_db <- tbl(wrds, I("crsp.stksecurityinfohist"))

# create lazy references to the CRSP tables on WRDS (nothing is downloaded yet; tbl() just points R at the SQL table so you can chain filter()/select()/inner_join() before finally calling collect() to actually pull data)
```

- Select **parameters** (those are the Tidy Finance ones)

```{r}
crsp_monthly <- msf_db %>% 
  filter(mthcaldt >= start_date & mthcaldt <= end_date) %>% 
  select(-c(siccd, primaryexch, conditionaltype, tradingstatusflg)) %>% # because both tables have those overlapping columns, drop em.
  inner_join(
    stksecurityinfohist_db %>% 
      filter(
        sharetype == "NS" & # ordinary/standard share class, excludes special share structures
          securitytype == "EQTY" & # security type equity 
          securitysubtype == "COM" & #security sub type common stock
          usincflg == "Y" & # US-incorporated only
          issuertype %in% c("ACOR", "CORP") & # issuers that are a corporation 
          primaryexch %in% c("N", "A", "Q") & # from NYSE, Amex, and NASDAQ
          conditionaltype %in% c("RW", "NW") & # keeping only months where the stock was trading under normal conditions 
          tradingstatusflg == "A" # actively traded stocks
      ) %>% 
      select(permno, secinfostartdt, secinfoenddt, primaryexch, siccd), # secinfostartdt = Security Info Start Date
    join_by(permno)
  ) %>% 
  filter(mthcaldt >= secinfostartdt & mthcaldt <= secinfoenddt) %>% # keep only months within permno-specific start dates (*)
  mutate(date = floor_date(mthcaldt, "month")) %>% # rounds a date down to the first day of its month
  select(
    permno, # Security identifier
    date, # Month of the observation
    ret = mthret, # Return
    shrout, # Shares outstanding (in thousands)
    prc = mthprc, # Last traded price in a month (use abs()?)
    primaryexch, # Primary exchange code
    siccd, # Industry code
    vol = mthvol # Trading volume - not from Tidy Finance - I added it
  ) %>% 
  collect() %>% 
  mutate(
    shrout = shrout * 1000 # CRSP reports shrout in thousands of shares natively- use this to put actual units
  )

# * a single permno can have multiple rows in stksecurityinfohist_db over its lifetime, each with a different secinfostartdt/secinfoenddt window, because a company's exchange listing, share type, or trading status can change over time (e.g., moves from NASDAQ to NYSE, or changes share class). This line keeps only the rows where the return's date actually falls inside the validity window of that particular classification record — i.e., "was this specific classification (exchange, share type, trading status) true at the time this return was observed?" Say permno 12345 was listed on NASDAQ  from 1990-01 to 1995-06 and moved to NYSE later on. stksecurityinfohist_db would have two rows for this permno, each with its own secinfostartdt/secinfoenddt. After the inner_join, a monthly return from, say, 1993-03 would get matched to both rows (since the join is only on permno). Without this date filter, you'd end up with duplicate rows for that month — one correctly reflecting "NASDAQ" and one incorrectly reflecting "NYSE" (which wasn't true yet in 1993). The mthcaldt >= secinfostartdt & mthcaldt <= secinfoenddt filter discards the incorrect match, keeping only the row where the classification was actually valid on that date.

# exclude price below $5?
```

- Create two mktcap variables (**mktcap, mktcap_lag**)

- Transform primary **listing exchange codes to explicit exchange names**

- Transform **industry codes to industry descriptions** (here following Bali et al. 2016 but can use FF 1997 too)

```{r}
# Adding mktcap variable

crsp_monthly <- crsp_monthly %>% 
  mutate(
    mktcap = shrout * prc / 10^6, # mktcap = price * nb of share outstanding - check if none prc are negative - divide mktcap by one million to make the units in million
    mktcap = na_if(mktcap, 0) # set zero market capitalization to missing as it makes conceptually little sense
  )

# Adding mktcap_lag variable

mktcap_lag <- crsp_monthly %>% 
  mutate(date = date %m+% months(1))  %>%  # use months(1) + join (not lag()) so a missing month produces a correct NA (sometimes jump in months in CRSP)
  select(permno, date, mktcap_lag = mktcap)
crsp_monthly <- crsp_monthly %>% 
  left_join(mktcap_lag, join_by(permno, date))

# Transform primary listing exchange codes to explicit exchange names

crsp_monthly <- crsp_monthly %>% 
  mutate(
    exchange = case_when(
      primaryexch == "N" ~ "NYSE",
      primaryexch == "A" ~ "AMEX",
      primaryexch == "Q" ~ "NASDAQ",
      .default = "Other"
    )
  ) %>% 
  select(-primaryexch)

# Transform industry codes to industry descriptions (here following Bali et al. (2016))

crsp_monthly <- crsp_monthly %>% 
  mutate(
    industry = case_when(
      siccd >= 1 & siccd <= 999 ~ "Agriculture",
      siccd >= 1000 & siccd <= 1499 ~ "Mining",
      siccd >= 1500 & siccd <= 1799 ~ "Construction",
      siccd >= 2000 & siccd <= 3999 ~ "Manufacturing",
      siccd >= 4000 & siccd <= 4899 ~ "Transportation",
      siccd >= 4900 & siccd <= 4999 ~ "Utilities",
      siccd >= 5000 & siccd <= 5199 ~ "Wholesale",
      siccd >= 5200 & siccd <= 5999 ~ "Retail",
      siccd >= 6000 & siccd <= 6799 ~ "Finance",
      siccd >= 7000 & siccd <= 8999 ~ "Services",
      siccd >= 9000 & siccd <= 9999 ~ "Public",
      .default = "Missing"
    )
  )
```

- Adding **excess return** (ret - rf (from ff3 database))

```{r}
ff3_rf <- read_parquet("data-r/factors_ff3_monthly.parquet") %>% 
  select(date, risk_free)

crsp_monthly <- crsp_monthly %>% 
  left_join(ff3_rf, join_by(date)) %>% 
  mutate(
    ret_excess = ret - risk_free
  ) %>% 
  select(-risk_free)
```

- **Drop NAs**

```{r}
crsp_monthly <- crsp_monthly %>% 
  drop_na(ret_excess, mktcap, mktcap_lag)
```

- **Write it** to save up some time (or don't and write instead **crsp_monthly_gvkey**)

```{r}
write_parquet(crsp_monthly, "data-r/crsp_monthly.parquet")
```

Works also for **daily price** (in a different way because way more rows) - <https://www.tidy-finance.org/r/wrds-crsp-and-compustat.html>

### 2) Compustat

Since info. mainly provided by 10-K, 10-Q etc..., unlike monthly CRPS, it's **annual data**

- Create a **lazy reference**

```{r}
funda_db <- tbl(wrds, I("comp.funda"))
```

- Select **parameters** (those are the Tidy Finance ones)

```{r}
compustat_annual <- funda_db %>%
  filter( # filter according the typical conventions
    indfmt == "INDL" & # get only records in industrial data format, which includes companies that are primarily involved in manufacturing, services, and other non-financial business activities
      datafmt == "STD" & # data in the standard format
      consol == "C" & # restricts to consolidated financial statements only
      curcd == "USD" & # in USD
      datadate >= start_date &
      datadate <= end_date  
  ) %>%
  select(
    gvkey, # Firm identifier
    datadate, # Date of the accounting data
    seq, # Stockholders' equity
    ceq, # Total common/ordinary equity
    at, # Total assets
    lt, # Total liabilities
    txditc, # Deferred taxes and investment tax credit
    txdb, # Deferred taxes
    itcb, # Investment tax credit
    pstkrv, # Preferred stock redemption value
    pstkl, # Preferred stock liquidating value
    pstk, # Preferred stock par value
    capx, # Capital investment
    oancf, # Operating cash flow
    sale, # Revenue
    cogs, # Costs of goods sold
    xint, # Interest expense
    xsga # Selling, general, and administrative expenses
  ) %>%
  collect()
```

- **Create variables** of book value of equity (**be**) and operating profitability (**op**) inspired by definitions in Ken French's data library

```{r}
compustat_annual <- compustat_annual %>%
  mutate(
    be = coalesce(seq, ceq + pstk, at - lt) + # coalesce returns the first non-missing value
      coalesce(txditc, txdb + itcb, 0) -
      coalesce(pstkrv, pstkl, pstk, 0),
    op = (sale - coalesce(cogs, 0) - coalesce(xsga, 0) - coalesce(xint, 0)) /
      be,
  )
```

- **Keep only the last available information for each firm-year group** (occasionally Compustat has multiple rows for the same gvkey + fiscal year — for example, a company might restate its financials, or there might be a duplicate record from a data correction)

```{r}
compustat_annual <- compustat_annual %>%
  mutate(year = year(datadate)) %>%
  group_by(gvkey, year) %>%
  filter(datadate == max(datadate)) %>%
  ungroup()
```

- **Compute the investment ratio inv** (according to Ken French’s variable definitions) as the change in total assets from one fiscal year to another

```{r}
compustat_annual <- compustat_annual %>%
  left_join(
    compustat_annual %>%
      select(gvkey, year, at_lag = at) %>%
      mutate(year = year + 1),
    join_by(gvkey, year)
  ) %>%
  mutate(
    inv = at / at_lag - 1,
    inv = if_else(at_lag <= 0, NA, inv)
  )

# not using lag() because  grabs "the previous row" within a gvkey group — it silently assumes the data is a clean, gapless sequence of consecutive fiscal years. But Compustat firm-year panels have gaps far more often than you might expect.
```

- **Write it** to save up some time

```{r}
write_parquet(compustat_annual, "data-r/compustat_annual.parquet")
```

### 3) Merging CRSP with Compustat

Link PERMNO with GVKEY

- Create a **lazy reference**

```{r}
ccm_linking_table_db <- tbl(wrds, I("crsp.ccmxpf_lnkhist"))
```

- Filter the **type**, **primary** **issuance** and **manage** '**still valid' date** that are NAs (Following Bali et al. (2016))

- So it creates a table with **PERMNO - GVKEY - BEG VALID PERIOD - END VALID PERIOD**

```{r}
ccm_linking_table <- ccm_linking_table_db %>%
  filter(
    linktype %in% c("LU", "LC") & # restricts to the two "reliable" link types LU and LC
      linkprim %in% c("P", "C") # restricts to links where the security is the firm's primary issue (P) or primary common share designated by CRSP (C).*
  ) %>%
  select(permno = lpermno, gvkey, linkdt, linkenddt) %>% # renames 'permno' for consistency and keeps linkdt/linkenddt — the validity window during which this permno-gvkey link was accurate (same secinfostartdt)
  collect() %>%
  mutate(linkenddt = replace_na(linkenddt, today())) #  for links that are still currently active, linkenddt is often stored as NA (meaning "still valid, no end date yet") rather than a far-future placeholder. This replaces those NAs with today's date, so that later date-range filtering (date >= linkdt & date <= linkenddt) works correctly for currently-active links instead of accidentally excluding them due to an NA comparison.

#  * This matters because a single Compustat firm (gvkey) can have multiple listed securities (e.g., different share classes), and you only want to match to the one that represents the company's main traded stock otherwise you'd double-count or mismatch a firm's accounting data against the wrong security.
```

- Create a table with all **PERMNO-DATE** pairs and **add the GVKEY** **corresponding** to each pair

```{r}
ccm_links <- crsp_monthly %>%
  inner_join(
    ccm_linking_table,
    join_by(permno),
    relationship = "many-to-many" # do not show warning is merging *
  ) %>%
  filter(
    !is.na(gvkey) & # drops any permno-months that have no corresponding Compustat firm at all 
      (date >= linkdt & date <= linkenddt) #  keeps only the link record that was actually valid on that specific month, discarding matches from a different, non-overlapping link history episode for the same permno.
  ) %>%
  select(permno, gvkey, date)

#* When you do inner_join(x, y, join_by(permno)), dplyr normally expects "one row in x matches at most one row in y" (one-to-one) or "one row in x matches many rows in y" (one-to-many). If your actual data doesn't fit that assumption, dplyr will throw a warning (not an error) telling you the join produced more rows than it expected, because both sides have multiple matching rows for the same key. It's not a filter and it doesn't change your results at all — it's purely a way of telling dplyr: "I know this join will produce multiple matches on both sides, I did this on purpose, don't warn me about it."
```

- **Add GVKEY** to **CRPS** database

```{r}
crsp_monthly_gvkey <- crsp_monthly %>% 
  left_join(ccm_links, join_by(permno, date))
```

- **Drop if NA** (not from Tidy Finance - I added it)

```{r}
crsp_monthly_gvkey <- crsp_monthly_gvkey %>%
  filter(!is.na(gvkey))
```

- **Write** **crsp_monthly_gvkey**

```{r}
write_parquet(crsp_monthly_gvkey, "data-r/crsp_monthly_gvkey.parquet")
```

- Don't merge CRSP and Compustat full because of lag accounting bias - that's why also keep the one year before. Remove it only at the very end.

# ─────────────────

# II/ Asset Pricing

## A) CAPM

According to the Capital Asset Pricing Model (CAPM) of Sharpe ([1964](https://www.tidy-finance.org/chapters/beta-estimation.html#ref-Sharpe1964)), Lintner ([1965](https://www.tidy-finance.org/chapters/beta-estimation.html#ref-Lintner1965)), and Mossin ([1966](https://www.tidy-finance.org/chapters/beta-estimation.html#ref-Mossin1966)), cross-sectional variation in expected asset returns should be a function of the covariance between the excess return of the asset and the excess return on the market portfolio. The regression coefficient of excess market returns on excess stock returns is usually called the market beta.

### 1) Libraries and Model

```{r}
library(slider) # rolling/sliding window calculations over time series (rolling regressions, rolling means, etc.)
library(nanoparquet)
#library(furrr) # parallel versions of purrr's map() functions — runs the same operation across many stocks simultaneously, using multiple CPU cores
```

The estimation procedure is based on a rolling-window estimation, where we may use either **monthly** or **daily returns** and different window lengths. To estimate the CAPM regression coefficients, we regress stock excess returns `ret_excess` on excess returns of the market portfolio `mkt_excess`.

![](images/clipboard-2146453621.png)

### 2) Prepare the Dataset for the Market Beta Regression

```{r}
crsp_mkt_beta <- read_parquet("data-r/crsp_monthly_gvkey.parquet") %>% 
  select(permno, date, industry, ret_excess) # keep industry for analytical purposes after the estimation

ff3_mktexcess <- read_parquet("data-r/factors_ff3_monthly.parquet") %>% 
  select(date, mkt_excess)

mkt_beta_data <- crsp_mkt_beta %>% 
  left_join(ff3_mktexcess, join_by(date))
```

### 3) Market Beta using Rolling-Window Estimation

```{r}
roll_capm_estimation <- function(data, look_back = 60, min_obs = 48) { #*  for each month you're estimating a beta at, look back 60 months (5 years) of that stock's return history to run the regression on, but only actually produce a beta if you have at least 48 valid observations in that window; otherwise return an empty tibble (skip) (no need to be consecutive months)
  cumulants <- data %>%
    summarize(
      n = n(),
      sum_x = sum(mkt_excess),
      sum_y = sum(ret_excess),
      sum_xx = sum(mkt_excess^2),
      sum_yy = sum(ret_excess^2),
      sum_xy = sum(mkt_excess * ret_excess),
      .by = c(permno, date)
    ) %>%
    arrange(permno, date) %>%
    mutate(
      period = year(date) * 12 + month(date),
      .by = permno
    )

  rolling_sums <- cumulants %>%
    mutate(
      across(
        c(n, sum_x, sum_y, sum_xx, sum_yy, sum_xy),
        \(col) slide_index_sum(col, period, before = look_back - 1)
      ),
      .by = permno
    ) %>%
    filter(n >= min_obs)

  estimates <- rolling_sums %>%
    mutate(
      s_xx = sum_xx - sum_x^2 / n,
      s_xy = sum_xy - sum_x * sum_y / n,
      s_yy = sum_yy - sum_y^2 / n,
      beta = s_xy / s_xx,
      alpha = (sum_y - beta * sum_x) / n,
      sigma2 = (s_yy - beta * s_xy) / (n - 2),
      t_alpha = alpha / sqrt(sigma2 * (1 / n + (sum_x / n)^2 / s_xx)),
      t_beta = beta / sqrt(sigma2 / s_xx)
    )

  bind_rows(
    estimates %>%
      transmute(
        permno,
        date,
        coefficient = "alpha",
        estimate = alpha,
        t_statistic = t_alpha
      ),
    estimates %>%
      transmute(
        permno,
        date,
        coefficient = "mkt_excess",
        estimate = beta,
        t_statistic = t_beta
      )
  ) %>%
    arrange(permno, date, coefficient) %>%
    as_tibble()
}

# Standard convention: the 60-month / 48-obs pairing is directly from Fama-MacBeth (1973) and has been carried through as the standard rolling-CAPM window in empirical asset pricing ever since. Some papers use 36/24 (shorter, more responsive to recent conditions) or 120/60 (longer, more stable) — but 60/48 is the classic default.
```

```{r}
capm_monthly <- roll_capm_estimation(mkt_beta_data)
capm_monthly
```

- Write it

```{r}
write_parquet(capm_monthly, "data-r/capm_monthly.parquet")
```

### 4) Expected Returns (for event study)

![](images/clipboard-4265857263.png)

```{r}
# keep only betas (remove alphas)
mkt_beta <- read_parquet("data-r/capm_monthly.parquet") %>%
  filter(coefficient == "mkt_excess") %>%
  select(permno, date, beta = estimate)

# Get risk-free and market excess return from FF3

ff3 <- read_parquet("data-r/factors_ff3_monthly.parquet") %>%
  select(date, risk_free, mkt_excess)
```

if you're building expected returns for an **event study / abnormal return** purpose, the standard convention is to use the **lagged beta** (estimated through month t−1, i.e., only information available *before* the month you're predicting). This avoids look-ahead bias — same principle as your `mktcap_lag` and 6-month `bm` lag: the expected return for month t should only use information knowable before t.

```{r}
expected_returns <- mkt_beta %>%
  mutate(date = date %m+% months(1)) %>% # shift beta forward: month t's expected return uses beta estimated through t-1
  left_join(ff3, join_by(date)) %>%
  mutate(exp_ret = risk_free + beta * mkt_excess) %>%
  select(permno, date, beta, exp_ret)
```

```{r}
abnormal_returns <- read_parquet("data-r/crsp_monthly_gvkey.parquet") %>%
  select(permno, date, ret) %>%
  inner_join(expected_returns, join_by(permno, date)) %>%
  mutate(ar = ret - exp_ret) # abnormal return = actual - expected
```

## B) Univariate Sorts and Monthly Premium (Size and BtM)

In this chapter, we dive into portfolio sorts, one of the most widely used statistical methodologies in empirical asset pricing (e.g., [Bali et al. 2016](https://www.tidy-finance.org/chapters/univariate-portfolio-sorts.html#ref-BaliEngleMurray2016)). The key application of portfolio sorts is to examine whether one or more variables can predict future excess returns. In general, the idea is to sort individual stocks into portfolios, where the stocks within each portfolio are similar with respect to a sorting variable, such as firm size.

### 1) Libraries and Data Preparation

```{r}
library(lmtest) # t-test and confidence intervals
library(broom) # converts lm()'s output into a clean little table of coefficient 
library(sandwich) # robust covariance matrix estimators
library(furrr)
library(rlang)
```

```{r}
crsp_univariate <- read_parquet("data-r/crsp_monthly_gvkey.parquet")
compustat_univariate <- read_parquet("data-r/compustat_annual.parquet")
```

### 2) Assign Portfolio Function

Function to separate in different portfolios (2 or +) based on the data, a sorting variable, a number of portfolio and the exchange(s).

```{r}
assign_portfolio <- function(
  data, # input 1
  sorting_variable, # input 2
  n_portfolios = NULL, # input 3: even splits (e.g. 2 -> median, 3 -> terciles); leave NULL if using percentiles
  percentiles = NULL, # input 4: explicit cuts (e.g. c(0.5) or c(0.3, 0.7) FF convention); leave NULL if using n_portfolios
  exchanges = NULL # input 5: optional - if NULL, use all exchanges (no filtering)
) {
  breakpoint_data <- data
  if (!is.null(exchanges)) {
    breakpoint_data <- breakpoint_data %>% 
      filter(exchange %in% exchanges) # e.g. NYSE-only breakpoints, standard FF convention (size AND bm)
  }

  probs <- if (!is.null(percentiles)) {
    c(0, percentiles, 1) # explicit cuts: add the two endpoints (0% and 100%) around your interior cut points
  } else {
    seq(0, 1, length.out = n_portfolios + 1) # even splits: rope logic - n pieces need n+1 marks
  }

  breakpoints <- breakpoint_data %>%
    pull({{ sorting_variable }}) %>% # curly-curly: extracts the column you specified without hard-coding its name
    quantile(
      probs = probs,
      na.rm = TRUE,
      names = FALSE
    )

  assigned_portfolios <- data %>%
    mutate(
      portfolio = findInterval( # for each stock's value, finds which bucket between the breakpoints it falls into
        pick(everything()) %>% pull({{ sorting_variable }}),
        breakpoints,
        all.inside = TRUE
      )
    ) %>%
    pull(portfolio) # returns the portfolio-number column as a plain vector

  assigned_portfolios
}
```

### 3) Assign 'Small Size' vs 'Big Size' Portfolios Accross Whole Sample (!= monthly)

- Based on mktcap_lag (variable already created)

```{r}
crsp_univariate <- crsp_univariate %>% 
    filter(!is.na(mktcap_lag))

size_sort <- assign_portfolio(crsp_univariate, sorting_variable = mktcap_lag, n_portfolios = 2, exchanges = c("NYSE", "NASDAQ", "AMEX")) # single vector function

crsp_univariate_size_sorted <- crsp_univariate %>%
  mutate(portfolio = size_sort) # attach vector back onto your data as a new column

crsp_univariate_size_sorted <- crsp_univariate_size_sorted %>%
  mutate(portfolio = factor(portfolio, levels = c(1, 2), labels = c("Small_Size", "Big_Size")))
```

### 4) Assign 'High Book-to-Market' vs 'Low Book-to-Market' Portfolios Accross Whole Sample (!= monthly)

- Based on Book-to-market (be_lag(6m)/mktcap_lag(1m))

- FF use 3 portfolios, low, medium and high

  Variable needed: be_lag (6 months lagged), mktcap_lag (one month lagged) and thus bm (be_lag / mktcap_lag)

  A fundamental problem in handling accounting data is the ***look-ahead bias*****;** we must not include data in forming a portfolio that is not public knowledge at the time. Of course, researchers have more information when looking into the past than agents had at that moment. However, abnormal excess returns from a trading strategy should not rely on an information advantage because the differential cannot be the result of informed agents’ trades. Hence, **we have to lag accounting information.** Book equity comes from **annual financial statements** (10-K filings), and there's a **real institutional delay** between a company's fiscal year-end and when that data is actually disclosed to the public (6 months)

- **Create** the **variable**

```{r}
# Make be > 0 and fix date
book_equity <- compustat_univariate %>% 
  select(gvkey, datadate, be) %>%
  filter(be > 0) %>% # best practice
  drop_na() %>%
  mutate(date = floor_date(ymd(datadate), "month")) # floor_date to set day = 1 - get only monthly data (instead of end on months)

# Create bm (6 months shifted)
bm_shifted <- book_equity %>%
  inner_join(crsp_univariate, join_by(gvkey, date)) %>%
  mutate(
    bm = be / mktcap_lag, # using mktcap_lag instead of mktcap
    sorting_date = date %m+% months(6),  # for bm lagged
    accounting_date = sorting_date # for below use
  ) %>%
  select(permno, gvkey, sorting_date, accounting_date, bm)

# Add bm to crps
crsp_univariate_bm <- crsp_univariate %>%
  left_join(bm_shifted, join_by(permno, gvkey, date == sorting_date)) %>% # join by sorting data (lagged one)
  arrange(permno, gvkey, date) %>%
  group_by(permno, gvkey) %>%
  fill(bm, accounting_date) %>% # fill() looks at each NA and replaces it with the most recent non-NA value above it, within each firm group. So the table becomes - recall compustat is annual and crsp monthly
  ungroup() %>%
  filter(accounting_date > date %m-% months(12)) %>% # keep the row only if the accounting data is less than 12 months old; drops firms that stopped reporting and would otherwise keep using stale bm forever
  select(-accounting_date) %>%
  drop_na()
```

- Call **assign_function**, attach vector back onto the data as a new column

```{r}
crsp_univariate_bm <- crsp_univariate_bm %>% 
  filter(!is.na(bm))

bm_sort <- assign_portfolio(crsp_univariate_bm, sorting_variable = bm, n_portfolios = 3, exchanges = c("NYSE", "NASDAQ", "AMEX")) # single vector function

crsp_univariate_bm_sorted <- crsp_univariate_bm %>%
  mutate(portfolio = bm_sort) # attach vector back onto your data as a new column

crsp_univariate_bm_sorted <- crsp_univariate_bm_sorted %>%
  mutate(portfolio = factor(portfolio, levels = c(1, 2, 3), labels = c("Low_BtM", "Medium_BtM", "High_BtM")))
```

### 5) Return Function

```{r}
calculate_returns <- function(ret_excess, mktcap_lag, value_weighted) {
  if (value_weighted) {
    weighted.mean(ret_excess, mktcap_lag, na.rm = TRUE) # value weighted technique if value_weighted = TRUE, otherwise equally weighted
  } else {
    mean(ret_excess, na.rm = TRUE)
  }
}

# Given a group of stocks (e.g., all stocks in "portfolio 3" in a given month (since monthly data)), this computes one representative return for that group.
```

### 6) SMB Monthly Premium

```{r}
compute_size_premium <- function(
  n_portfolios = 2,
  exchanges = c("NYSE", "NASDAQ", "AMEX"),
  value_weighted = TRUE,
  data = crsp_univariate,
  monthly = FALSE # TRUE returns the full monthly series; FALSE returns the sample average
) {
  portfolio_returns <- data %>%
    group_by(date) %>% # fresh breakpoints every month (essential - size distribution shifts over decades)
    mutate(
      portfolio = assign_portfolio(
        data = pick(everything()),
        sorting_variable = mktcap_lag,
        n_portfolios = n_portfolios,
        exchanges = exchanges
      )
    ) %>%
    group_by(date, portfolio) %>%
    summarize(
      ret = calculate_returns(ret_excess, mktcap_lag, value_weighted),
      .groups = "drop_last"
    ) %>%
    summarize(
      size_premium = ret[portfolio == min(portfolio)] - # Small
        ret[portfolio == max(portfolio)],                # Big
      .groups = "drop"
    )

  if (monthly) {
    portfolio_returns # one row per month: the monthly SMB-style series
  } else {
    portfolio_returns %>%
      summarize(size_premium = mean(size_premium, na.rm = TRUE))
  }
}
```

```{r}
smb_monthly <- compute_size_premium(data = crsp_univariate, monthly = TRUE)
```

### 7) HML Monthly Premium

```{r}
compute_value_premium <- function(
  n_portfolios = 3,
  exchanges = c("NYSE", "NASDAQ", "AMEX"),
  value_weighted = TRUE,
  data = crsp_univariate_bm,
  monthly = FALSE
) {
  portfolio_returns <- data %>%
    group_by(date) %>%
    mutate(
      portfolio = assign_portfolio(
        data = pick(everything()),
        sorting_variable = bm,
        n_portfolios = n_portfolios,
        exchanges = exchanges
      )
    ) %>%
    group_by(date, portfolio) %>%
    summarize(
      ret = calculate_returns(ret_excess, mktcap_lag, value_weighted),
      .groups = "drop_last"
    ) %>%
    summarize(
      value_premium = ret[portfolio == max(portfolio)] - # High BtM (note: flipped vs size)
        ret[portfolio == min(portfolio)],                 # Low BtM
      .groups = "drop"
    )

  if (monthly) {
    portfolio_returns
  } else {
    portfolio_returns %>%
      summarize(value_premium = mean(value_premium, na.rm = TRUE))
  }
}
```

```{r}
hml_monthly <- compute_value_premium(data = crsp_univariate_bm, monthly = TRUE)
```

## C) Bivariate Sorts and Monthly Premium (Size and BtM)

### 1) Data Preparation

```{r}
factors_ff3_monthly <- download_data( # to check accuracy
  domain = "famafrench",
  dataset = "Fama/French 3 Factors",
  start_date = start_date,
  end_date = end_date
)

crsp_monthly_bivariate <- read_parquet("data-r/crsp_monthly_gvkey.parquet") %>% 
  select(permno, gvkey, date, ret_excess, mktcap, mktcap_lag, exchange) %>% 
  drop_na()
```

### 3) Create the Variables and the Dataset

```{r}
book_equity <- read_parquet("data-r/compustat_annual.parquet") %>% 
  select(gvkey, datadate, be) %>% 
  filter(be > 0) %>% 
  drop_na() %>% 
  mutate(date = floor_date(ymd(datadate), "month"))

size_shifted <- crsp_monthly_bivariate %>% 
  mutate(sorting_date = date %m+% months(1)) %>% 
  select(permno, sorting_date, size = mktcap)

bm_shifted <- book_equity %>% 
  inner_join(crsp_monthly_bivariate, join_by(gvkey, date)) %>% 
  mutate(
    bm = be / mktcap,
    sorting_date = date %m+% months(6),
    accounting_date = sorting_date
  ) %>% 
  select(permno, gvkey, sorting_date, accounting_date, bm)
```

- Join bm and size from before

```{r}

bivariate_data <- crsp_monthly_bivariate %>%
  left_join(bm_shifted, join_by(permno, gvkey, date == sorting_date)) %>%
  left_join(size_shifted, join_by(permno, date == sorting_date)) %>%
  select(permno, gvkey, date, ret_excess, mktcap_lag, size, bm, exchange, accounting_date) %>%
  arrange(permno, gvkey, date) %>%
  group_by(permno, gvkey) %>%
  fill(bm, accounting_date) %>% # carry bm forward until next annual report
  ungroup() %>%
  filter(accounting_date > date %m-% months(12)) %>% # drop stale accounting data
  select(-accounting_date) %>%
  drop_na()
```

### 3) Independent vs Dependent Sort

Bivariate sorts = sorting stocks on **two characteristics at the same time**, creating a grid of portfolios instead of a line. **Characteristics are correlated**. Small firms tend to have higher book-to-market; value firms tend to be smaller. So when your univariate BM sort shows high-BM stocks outperforming, a skeptic asks: *is that a value effect, or just the size effect wearing a costume?* A univariate sort can't answer — its "High BM" bucket is contaminated with smallness. Bivariate sorts are the fix: examine one variable **while holding the other one fixed**.

The mechanics — a 2×3 size × BM sort

1)  Sort on size → Small / Big

2)  Sort on BM → Low / Medium / High

- Independent: BM breakpoints on the FULL universe (blind to step 1)

- Dependent: BM breakpoints WITHIN each size group (cells created directly here)

3)  Intersect → every stock lands in exactly one of 6 cells (Independent only. Dependent: no step — step 2 already placed everyone.)

![](images/clipboard-992846729.png)

4)  Compute each cell's (value-weighted) monthly return

HML_t = avg(S/H_t, B/H_t) − avg(S/L_t, B/L_t)

SMB_t = avg(S/L_t S/M_t, S/H_t) − avg(B/L_t, B/M_t, B/H_t)

### 4) Independent Sorts and Monthly Premium (Size and BtM)

```{r}
# 1) Assign both dimensions each month (independent sort: both breakpoints on the full cross-section)
portfolios_2x3_indep <- bivariate_data %>%
  group_by(date) %>%
  mutate(
    portfolio_size = assign_portfolio(
      data = pick(everything()),
      sorting_variable = size,
      n_portfolios = 2, # Small / Big (median)
      exchanges = c("NYSE")
    ),
    portfolio_bm = assign_portfolio(
      data = pick(everything()),
      sorting_variable = bm,
      n_portfolios = 3, # Low / Medium / High
      exchanges = c("NYSE")
    )
  ) %>%
# 2) Intersect (independent sort) -> 6 cells, compute each cell's value-weighted monthly return
  group_by(date, portfolio_bm, portfolio_size) %>% 
  summarize(
    ret = weighted.mean(ret_excess, mktcap_lag),
    .groups = "drop"
  )
# 3) Build the monthly factors from the 6 cells
factors_replicated_indep <- portfolios_2x3_indep %>%
  group_by(date) %>%
  summarize(
    # HML_t = avg(S/H_t, B/H_t) - avg(S/L_t, B/L_t)   (medium column unused)
    hml_replicated = mean(ret[portfolio_bm == 3]) - mean(ret[portfolio_bm == 1]),
    # SMB_t = avg(S/L_t, S/M_t, S/H_t) - avg(B/L_t, B/M_t, B/H_t)
    smb_replicated = mean(ret[portfolio_size == 1]) - mean(ret[portfolio_size == 2])
  )
```

### 5) Compare with Actual Premiums (independent)

```{r}
comparison <- factors_ff3_monthly %>%
  select(date, smb, hml) %>%
  inner_join(factors_replicated_indep, join_by(date))

comparison %>%
  summarise(
    cor_smb = cor(smb, smb_replicated),
    cor_hml = cor(hml, hml_replicated),
    mean_smb_official = mean(smb), mean_smb_yours = mean(smb_replicated),
    mean_hml_official = mean(hml), mean_hml_yours = mean(hml_replicated)
  )
```

### 6) Dependent Sorts and Monthly Premium (Size and BtM)

```{r}
portfolios_2x3_dep <- bivariate_data %>%
  group_by(date) %>%
  mutate(
    portfolio_size = assign_portfolio(
      data = pick(everything()),
      sorting_variable = size,
      n_portfolios = 2,
      exchanges = c("NYSE")
    )
  ) %>%
  group_by(date, portfolio_size) %>%  # <- THE difference between independent sort and dependent sort: regroup before the second sort
  mutate(
    portfolio_bm = assign_portfolio(
      data = pick(everything()),
      sorting_variable = bm,
      n_portfolios = 3,
      exchanges = c("NYSE")
    )
  ) %>%
  group_by(date, portfolio_size, portfolio_bm) %>%
  summarize(
    ret = weighted.mean(ret_excess, mktcap_lag),
    .groups = "drop"
  )

factors_replicated_dep <- portfolios_2x3_dep %>%
  group_by(date) %>%
  summarize(
    # HML_t (conditional) = avg(S/H_t, B/H_t) - avg(S/L_t, B/L_t)
    hml_dep = mean(ret[portfolio_bm == 3]) - mean(ret[portfolio_bm == 1]),
    # SMB_t (conditional) = avg(S/L_t, S/M_t, S/H_t) - avg(B/L_t, B/M_t, B/H_t)
    smb_dep = mean(ret[portfolio_size == 1]) - mean(ret[portfolio_size == 2])
  )

```

### 7) Compare with Actual Premiums (dependent)

```{r}
comparison <- factors_ff3_monthly %>%
  select(date, smb, hml) %>%
  inner_join(factors_replicated_dep, join_by(date))

comparison %>%
  summarise(
    cor_smb = cor(smb, smb_dep),
    cor_hml = cor(hml, hml_dep),
    mean_smb_official = mean(smb), mean_smb_yours = mean(smb_dep),
    mean_hml_official = mean(hml), mean_hml_yours = mean(hml_dep)
  )
```

A little smaller than independent - that's normla FF3 use independent sorting :)

## D) Replicating Fama-French Three Factors Premium

- Like C) but with some more precise parameters

### 1) Data Preparation

```{r}
crsp_monthly_replication_3 <- read_parquet("data-r/crsp_monthly_gvkey.parquet") %>% 
  select(permno, gvkey,date,ret_excess,mktcap,mktcap_lag,exchange)

compustat_annual_replication_3  <- read_parquet("data-r/compustat_annual.parquet")  %>% 
  select(gvkey, datadate, be)  %>% 
  filter(be > 0)

factors_ff3_monthly <- download_data( # to compare
  domain = "famafrench",
  dataset = "Fama/French 3 Factors",
  start_date = start_date,
  end_date = end_date
)
```

First, Fama and French **form their portfolios in June of year t**, whereby the returns of July are the first monthly return for the respective portfolio. For firm size, they consequently use the market capitalization recorded for June. It is then held constant until June of year t+1.

Second, Fama and French also have a different protocol for computing the book-to-market ratio. **They use market equity as of the end of year t-1 and the book equity reported in year, i.e., the datadate is within the last year**. Hence, the book-to-market ratio can be based on accounting information that is up to 18 months old. Market equity also does not necessarily reflect the same time point as book equity. The other sorting variables are analogously to book equity taken from year t-1.

### 2) Create the Variables and the Dataset

```{r}
size <- crsp_monthly_replication_3 %>%
  filter(month(date) == 6) %>%
  mutate(sorting_date = date %m+% months(1)) %>%
  select(permno, exchange, sorting_date, size = mktcap)

market_equity <- crsp_monthly_replication_3 %>%
  filter(month(date) == 12) %>%
  mutate(sorting_date = ymd(str_c(year(date) + 1, "0701"))) %>%
  select(permno, gvkey, sorting_date, me = mktcap)

book_to_market <- compustat_annual_replication_3 %>%
  mutate(sorting_date = ymd(str_c(year(datadate) + 1, "0701"))) %>%
  select(gvkey, sorting_date, be) %>%
  inner_join(market_equity, join_by(gvkey, sorting_date)) %>%
  mutate(bm = be / me) %>%
  select(permno, sorting_date, me, bm)

sorting_variables_replication_3 <- size %>%
  inner_join(
    book_to_market,
    join_by(permno, sorting_date)
  ) %>%
  drop_na() %>%
  distinct(permno, sorting_date, .keep_all = TRUE)
```

### 3) Portfolio Independent Sort (using assign_portfolio)

Fama and French rely on NYSE-specific breakpoints to **independently** form two portfolios in the size dimension at the median

And three portfolios in the dimension of book-to-market at the 30- and 70-percentiles (also NYSE only)

```{r}
portfolios_replication_3 <- sorting_variables %>%
  group_by(sorting_date) %>%
  mutate(
    portfolio_size = assign_portfolio(
      data = pick(everything()),
      sorting_variable = size,
      percentiles = c(0.5),
      exchanges = "NYSE",
    ),
    portfolio_bm = assign_portfolio(
      data = pick(everything()),
      sorting_variable = bm,
      percentiles = c(0.3, 0.7),
      exchanges = "NYSE",
    )
  ) %>%
  ungroup() %>%
  select(permno, sorting_date, portfolio_size, portfolio_bm)
```

### 4) Merge the Portfolios to the Data for the Rest of the Year

```{r}
portfolios_replication_3 <- crsp_monthly_replication_3 %>%
  mutate(
    sorting_date = case_when(
      month(date) <= 6 ~ ymd(str_c(year(date) - 1, "0701")),
      month(date) >= 7 ~ ymd(str_c(year(date), "0701"))
    )
  ) %>%
  inner_join(portfolios_replication_3, join_by(permno, sorting_date))
```

### 5) Compute the Value-Weighted Average Return for Each of the Six Portfolios

```{r}
factors_replicated_3 <- portfolios_replication_3 %>%
  group_by(portfolio_size, portfolio_bm, date) %>%
  summarize(
    ret = weighted.mean(ret_excess, mktcap_lag),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) %>%
  group_by(date) %>%
  summarize(
    smb_replicated_3 = mean(ret[portfolio_size == 1]) -
      mean(ret[portfolio_size == 2]),
    hml_replicated_3 = mean(ret[portfolio_bm == 3]) -
      mean(ret[portfolio_bm == 1])
  )
```

### 6) Compare with Actual FF3 Premiums

```{r}
comparison <- factors_ff3_monthly %>%
  select(date, smb, hml) %>%
  inner_join(factors_replicated_3, join_by(date))

comparison %>%
  summarise(
    cor_smb = cor(smb, smb_replicated_3),
    cor_hml = cor(hml, hml_replicated_3),
    mean_smb_official = mean(smb), mean_smb_yours = mean(smb_replicated_3),
    mean_hml_official = mean(hml), mean_hml_yours = mean(hml_replicated_3)
  )
```

Very good results!

## E) Replicating Fama-French Five Factors Premium

### 1) Data Preparation

```{r}
crsp_monthly_replication_5 <- read_parquet("data-r/crsp_monthly_gvkey.parquet") %>% 
  select(permno, gvkey,date,ret_excess,mktcap,mktcap_lag,exchange)

compustat_annual_replication_5  <- read_parquet("data-r/compustat_annual.parquet")  %>% 
  select(gvkey, datadate, be, op, inv)  %>% 
  filter(be > 0)

factors_ff5_monthly <- download_data( # to compare
  domain = "famafrench",
  dataset = "factors_ff_5_2x3_monthly",
  start_date = start_date,
  end_date = end_date
)
```

### 2) Create the Variables and the Dataset

```{r}
# Recompute the first 2 variables
size <- crsp_monthly_replication_5 %>%
  filter(month(date) == 6) %>%
  mutate(sorting_date = date %m+% months(1)) %>%
  select(permno, exchange, sorting_date, size = mktcap)

market_equity <- crsp_monthly_replication_5 %>%
  filter(month(date) == 12) %>%
  mutate(sorting_date = ymd(str_c(year(date) + 1, "0701"))) %>%
  select(permno, gvkey, sorting_date, me = mktcap)

# Compute the two more (+bm)

other_sorting_variables <- compustat_annual_replication_5 %>%
  mutate(sorting_date = ymd(str_c(year(datadate) + 1, "0701"))) %>%
  select(gvkey, sorting_date, be, op, inv) %>%
  inner_join(market_equity, join_by(gvkey, sorting_date)) %>%
  mutate(bm = be / me) %>%
  select(permno, sorting_date, me, be, bm, op, inv)

sorting_variables_replication_5 <- size %>%
  inner_join(
    other_sorting_variables,
    join_by(permno, sorting_date)
  ) %>%
  drop_na() %>%
  distinct(permno, sorting_date, .keep_all = TRUE)
```

### 3) Portfolio Independent and Dependent Sorts (using assign_portfolio)

In each month, we independently sort all stocks into the two size portfolios. The value, profitability, and investment portfolios, on the other hand, are the results of dependent sorts based on the size portfolios. We then merge the portfolios to the return data for the rest of the year just as above.

```{r}
portfolios <- sorting_variables_replication_5 %>%
  group_by(sorting_date) %>%
  mutate(
    portfolio_size = assign_portfolio(
      data = pick(everything()),
      sorting_variable = "size",
      percentiles = c(0.5),
      exchanges = "NYSE"
    )
  ) %>%
  group_by(sorting_date, portfolio_size) %>%
  mutate(
    across(
      c(bm, op, inv),
      ~ assign_portfolio(
        data = pick(everything()),
        sorting_variable = .,
        percentiles = c(0.3, 0.7),
        exchanges = "NYSE"
      ),
      .names = "portfolio_{.col}"
    )
  ) %>%
  ungroup() %>%
  select(
    permno,
    sorting_date,
    portfolio_size,
    portfolio_bm,
    portfolio_op,
    portfolio_inv
  )

portfolios_replication_5 <- crsp_monthly_replication_5 %>%
  mutate(
    sorting_date = case_when(
      month(date) <= 6 ~ ymd(str_c(year(date) - 1, "0701")),
      month(date) >= 7 ~ ymd(str_c(year(date), "0701"))
    )
  ) %>%
  inner_join(portfolios, join_by(permno, sorting_date))
```

### 4) Create All Factors and Calculate Premiums

Now, we want to construct each of the factors, but this time the size factor actually comes last because it is the result of averaging across all other factor portfolios. This dependency is the reason why we keep the table with value-weighted portfolio returns as a separate object that we reuse later. We construct the value factor, HML, as above by going long the two portfolios with high book-to-market ratios and shorting the two portfolios with low book-to-market.

- Monthly Value Premium (HML)

Going long the two portfolios with high book-to-market ratios and shorting the two portfolios with low book-to-market.

```{r}
portfolios_value_5 <- portfolios_replication_5 %>%
  group_by(portfolio_size, portfolio_bm, date) %>%
  summarize(
    ret = weighted.mean(ret_excess, mktcap_lag),
    .groups = "drop"
  )

factors_value_5 <- portfolios_value_5 %>%
  group_by(date) %>%
  summarize(
    hml_replicated_5 = mean(ret[portfolio_bm == 3]) -
      mean(ret[portfolio_bm == 1])
  )
```

- Monthly Profitability Premium (RMW)

Take a long position in the two high profitability portfolios and a short position in the two low profitability portfolios.

```{r}
portfolios_profitability_5 <- portfolios_replication_5 %>%
  group_by(portfolio_size, portfolio_op, date) %>%
  summarize(
    ret = weighted.mean(ret_excess, mktcap_lag),
    .groups = "drop"
  )

factors_profitability_5 <- portfolios_profitability_5 %>%
  group_by(date) %>%
  summarize(
    rmw_replicated_5 = mean(ret[portfolio_op == 3]) -
      mean(ret[portfolio_op == 1])
  )
```

- Monthly Investment Premium (CMA)

We go long the two low investment portfolios and short the two high investment portfolios.

```{r}
portfolios_investment_5 <- portfolios_replication_5 %>%
  group_by(portfolio_size, portfolio_inv, date) %>%
  summarize(
    ret = weighted.mean(ret_excess, mktcap_lag),
    .groups = "drop"
  )

factors_investment_5 <- portfolios_investment_5 %>%
  group_by(date) %>%
  summarize(
    cma_replicated_5 = mean(ret[portfolio_inv == 1]) -
      mean(ret[portfolio_inv == 3])
  )
```

- Monthly Size Premium (SMB)

Going long the nine small portfolios and short the nine large portfolios.

```{r}
factors_size_5 <- bind_rows(
  portfolios_value_5,
  portfolios_profitability_5,
  portfolios_investment_5
) %>%
  group_by(date) %>%
  summarize(
    smb_replicated_5 = mean(ret[portfolio_size == 1]) -
      mean(ret[portfolio_size == 2])
  )
```

### 5) Merge Them

```{r}
factors_replicated_5 <- factors_size_5 %>%
  full_join(factors_value_5, join_by(date)) %>%
  full_join(factors_profitability_5, join_by(date)) %>%
  full_join(factors_investment_5, join_by(date))
```

### 6) Compare with Actual FF5 Premiums

```{r}
comparison <- factors_ff5_monthly %>%
  select(date, smb, hml,rmw,cma) %>%
  inner_join(factors_replicated_5, join_by(date))

comparison %>%
  summarise(
    # correlations - the machinery check
    cor_smb = cor(smb, smb_replicated_5, use = "complete.obs"),
    cor_hml = cor(hml, hml_replicated_5, use = "complete.obs"),
    cor_rmw = cor(rmw, rmw_replicated_5, use = "complete.obs"),
    cor_cma = cor(cma, cma_replicated_5, use = "complete.obs"),
    # means - the premium-level check
    mean_smb_official = mean(smb), mean_smb_yours = mean(smb_replicated_5),
    mean_hml_official = mean(hml), mean_hml_yours = mean(hml_replicated_5),
    mean_rmw_official = mean(rmw), mean_rmw_yours = mean(rmw_replicated_5),
    mean_cma_official = mean(cma), mean_cma_yours = mean(cma_replicated_5))
```

All great!!

## F) Fama-French Three-Factor Model

### 1) Libraries and Model

```{r}
library(slider) # rolling/sliding window calculations over time series (rolling regressions, rolling means, etc.)
library(nanoparquet)
```

![](images/clipboard-1229676446.png)

### 2) Prepare the Dataset for the Market, Size and B/M Betas Regressions

```{r}
crsp_ff3_beta <- read_parquet("data-r/crsp_monthly_gvkey.parquet") %>% 
  select(permno, date, industry, ret_excess) # keep industry for analytical purposes after the estimation

factors_ff3_beta <- read_parquet("data-r/factors_ff3_monthly.parquet") %>% 
    select(date, mkt_excess, smb, hml)

ff3_betas_data <- crsp_ff3_beta %>% 
  left_join(factors_ff3_beta, join_by(date))
```

### 3) Market, Size and B/M Betas using Rolling-Window Estimation

```{r}
roll_ff3_estimation <- function(data, look_back = 60, min_obs = 48) {
  # x1 = mkt_excess, x2 = smb, x3 = hml, y = ret_excess

  cumulants <- data %>%
    summarize(
      n = n(),
      sum_x1 = sum(mkt_excess), sum_x2 = sum(smb), sum_x3 = sum(hml),
      sum_y = sum(ret_excess),
      sum_x1x1 = sum(mkt_excess^2), sum_x2x2 = sum(smb^2), sum_x3x3 = sum(hml^2),
      sum_x1x2 = sum(mkt_excess * smb),
      sum_x1x3 = sum(mkt_excess * hml),
      sum_x2x3 = sum(smb * hml),
      sum_x1y = sum(mkt_excess * ret_excess),
      sum_x2y = sum(smb * ret_excess),
      sum_x3y = sum(hml * ret_excess),
      sum_yy = sum(ret_excess^2),
      .by = c(permno, date)
    ) %>%
    arrange(permno, date) %>%
    mutate(period = year(date) * 12 + month(date), .by = permno)

  rolling_sums <- cumulants %>%
    mutate(
      across(
        c(n, starts_with("sum_")),
        \(col) slide_index_sum(col, period, before = look_back - 1)
      ),
      .by = permno
    ) %>%
    filter(n >= min_obs)

  estimates <- rolling_sums %>%
    mutate(
      # centered (demeaned) cross-products: s_jk = Σxjxk − Σxj·Σxk/n
      s11 = sum_x1x1 - sum_x1^2 / n,
      s22 = sum_x2x2 - sum_x2^2 / n,
      s33 = sum_x3x3 - sum_x3^2 / n,
      s12 = sum_x1x2 - sum_x1 * sum_x2 / n,
      s13 = sum_x1x3 - sum_x1 * sum_x3 / n,
      s23 = sum_x2x3 - sum_x2 * sum_x3 / n,
      s1y = sum_x1y - sum_x1 * sum_y / n,
      s2y = sum_x2y - sum_x2 * sum_y / n,
      s3y = sum_x3y - sum_x3 * sum_y / n,
      syy = sum_yy - sum_y^2 / n,

      # cofactors of the symmetric 3x3 matrix S (for Cramer's rule / inverse)
      adj11 = s22 * s33 - s23^2,
      adj12 = s13 * s23 - s12 * s33,
      adj13 = s12 * s23 - s13 * s22,
      adj22 = s11 * s33 - s13^2,
      adj23 = s12 * s13 - s11 * s23,
      adj33 = s11 * s22 - s12^2,
      det = s11 * adj11 + s12 * adj12 + s13 * adj13,

      # betas: b = S^{-1} s_y
      beta_mkt = (adj11 * s1y + adj12 * s2y + adj13 * s3y) / det,
      beta_smb = (adj12 * s1y + adj22 * s2y + adj23 * s3y) / det,
      beta_hml = (adj13 * s1y + adj23 * s2y + adj33 * s3y) / det,

      # alpha from the means
      alpha = (sum_y - beta_mkt * sum_x1 - beta_smb * sum_x2 - beta_hml * sum_x3) / n,

      # residual variance: SSR/(n − 4) (4 estimated params: alpha + 3 betas)
      sigma2 = (syy - beta_mkt * s1y - beta_smb * s2y - beta_hml * s3y) / (n - 4),

      # standard errors: var(b_j) = sigma2 * [S^{-1}]_jj
      t_mkt = beta_mkt / sqrt(sigma2 * adj11 / det),
      t_smb = beta_smb / sqrt(sigma2 * adj22 / det),
      t_hml = beta_hml / sqrt(sigma2 * adj33 / det),

      # t of alpha: var(alpha) = sigma2 * (1/n + m' S^{-1} m), m = vector of regressor means
      m1 = sum_x1 / n, m2 = sum_x2 / n, m3 = sum_x3 / n,
      quad_form = (m1^2 * adj11 + m2^2 * adj22 + m3^2 * adj33 +
                   2 * m1 * m2 * adj12 + 2 * m1 * m3 * adj13 + 2 * m2 * m3 * adj23) / det,
      t_alpha = alpha / sqrt(sigma2 * (1 / n + quad_form))
    )

  bind_rows(
    estimates %>% transmute(permno, date, coefficient = "alpha",      estimate = alpha,    t_statistic = t_alpha),
    estimates %>% transmute(permno, date, coefficient = "mkt_excess", estimate = beta_mkt, t_statistic = t_mkt),
    estimates %>% transmute(permno, date, coefficient = "smb",        estimate = beta_smb, t_statistic = t_smb),
    estimates %>% transmute(permno, date, coefficient = "hml",        estimate = beta_hml, t_statistic = t_hml)
  ) %>%
    arrange(permno, date, coefficient) %>%
    as_tibble()
}
```

```{r}
ff3_betas <- roll_ff3_estimation(ff3_betas_data)
ff3_betas
```

```{r}

```

```{r}
# keep only the three betas (drop alphas), reshape wide
ff3_betas_wide <- read_parquet("data-r/ff3_betas.parquet") %>%
  filter(coefficient != "alpha") %>%
  select(permno, date, coefficient, estimate) %>%
  pivot_wider(names_from = coefficient, values_from = estimate, names_prefix = "beta_") %>%

ff3 <- read_parquet("data-r/factors_ff3_monthly.parquet") %>%

```

```{r}
expected_returns_ff3 <- ff3_betas_wide %>%
  mutate(date = date %m+% months(1)) %>% # lag betas: month t's E[r] uses betas estimated through t-1 (no look-ahead)
  left_join(ff3, join_by(date)) %>%
  mutate(
    exp_ret = risk_free +
      beta_mkt * mkt_excess +
      beta_smb * smb +
      beta_hml * hml # E[r] = rf + b1(rm-rf) + b2·SMB + b3·HML
  ) %>%
  select(permno, date, exp_ret)
```

## G) Fama-MacBeth Regressions (here using FF3)

**Fama-MacBeth is a general econometric procedure, not a specific asset pricing model.** It's the *testing machinery*, and CAPM/FF3/FF5/q5 are the *models being tested*. You can plug any of them (or your own custom factors/characteristics) into the same two-step framework.

Researchers use the two-stage regression approach to estimate risk premiums in various markets, but predominately in the stock market.

### 1) Libraries Data Preparation

```{r}
library(sandwich) # robust covariance matrix estimators
library(broom) # converts lm()'s output into a clean little table of coefficient 
```

We illustrate Fama and MacBeth ([1973](https://www.tidy-finance.org/chapters/fama-macbeth-regressions.html#ref-Fama1973)) with the monthly CRSP sample and use three characteristics to explain the cross-section of returns: market capitalization, the book-to-market ratio, and the CAPM beta.

```{r}
crsp_monthly_fama_macbeth <- read_parquet("data-r/crsp_monthly_gvkey.parquet") %>% 
  select(permno, gvkey, date, ret_excess, mktcap) %>% 
  collect()

compustat_fama_macbeth <- read_parquet("data-r/compustat_annual.parquet") %>% 
  select(datadate, gvkey, be) %>% 
  filter(be > 0)

betas_fama_macbeth <- read_parquet("data-r/capm_monthly.parquet") %>%
  filter(coefficient == "mkt_excess") %>%
  select(permno, date, beta = estimate)
```

- **Compute** the **book-to-market ratio** and the (log) **market capitalization and create** the Fama-Mcbeth **dataset**

```{r}
characteristics <- compustat_fama_macbeth %>% 
  mutate(date = floor_date(ymd(datadate), "month")) %>% 
  left_join(crsp_monthly_fama_macbeth, join_by(gvkey, date)) %>% 
  left_join(betas_fama_macbeth, join_by(permno, date)) %>% 
  transmute(
    gvkey,
    bm = be / mktcap,
    log_mktcap = log(mktcap),
    beta = beta,
    sorting_date = date %m+% months(6)
  )

data_fama_macbeth <- crsp_monthly_fama_macbeth %>% 
  left_join(characteristics, join_by(gvkey, date == sorting_date)) %>% 
  group_by(permno) %>% 
  arrange(date) %>% 
  fill(c(beta, bm, log_mktcap), .direction = "down") %>% 
  ungroup() %>% 
  left_join(
    crsp_monthly_fama_macbeth %>% 
      select(permno, date, ret_excess_lead = ret_excess) %>% 
      mutate(date = date %m-% months(1)),
    join_by(permno, date)
  ) %>% 
  select(permno, date, ret_excess_lead, beta, log_mktcap, bm) %>% 
  drop_na()
```

### 2) Cross-Sectional Regression (estimate γ\*\* for each characteristic\*\*)

First, we run the cross-sectional regressions with the characteristics as explanatory variables for each month. We regress the returns of the test assets at a particular time point on the characteristics of each asset. By doing so, **we get an ESTIMATE of the risk premiums γ** for each point in time.

![](images/clipboard-2811317808.png)

```{r}
risk_premiums <- data_fama_macbeth %>% 
  nest(data = c(ret_excess_lead, beta, log_mktcap, bm, permno)) %>% # create mini table per month for easier lm()
  mutate(
    estimates = map( # run one regression across its stocks for each mini table to find γ of beta, log_mktcap and bm
      data,
      \(x) tidy(lm(ret_excess_lead ~ beta + log_mktcap + bm, data = x)) # tidy() (from broom) just converts lm()'s output into a clean little table of coefficient 
    )
  ) %>% 
  unnest(estimates) # Stacks all those monthly coefficient tables back into one long table
```

### 3) Time-series Aggregation (expected **γ** for each characteristic)

Now that we have the risk premiums’ estimates for each period, we can average across the time-series dimension to get the expected risk premium for each characteristic.

```{r}
price_of_risk <- risk_premiums %>% 
  group_by(factor = term) %>% 
  summarize(
    risk_premium = mean(estimate),
    t_statistic = mean(estimate) / sd(estimate) * sqrt(n())
  )
```

### 4) Adjust for autocorrelation

It is common to adjust for autocorrelation when reporting standard errors of risk premiums. As in [Univariate Portfolio Sorts](https://www.tidy-finance.org/chapters/univariate-portfolio-sorts.html), the typical procedure for this is computing Newey and West ([1987](https://www.tidy-finance.org/chapters/fama-macbeth-regressions.html#ref-Newey1987)) standard errors.

We again recommend the data-driven approach of Newey and West ([1994](https://www.tidy-finance.org/chapters/fama-macbeth-regressions.html#ref-Newey1994)) using the `NeweyWest()` function, but note that you can enforce the typical 6 lag settings via `NeweyWest(., lag = 6, prewhite = FALSE)`.

```{r}
regressions_for_newey_west <- risk_premiums %>% 
  select(date, factor = term, estimate) %>% 
  nest(data = c(date, estimate)) %>% 
  mutate(
    model = map(data, \(x) lm(estimate ~ 1, x)),
    mean = map(model, tidy)
  )

price_of_risk_newey_west <- regressions_for_newey_west %>% 
  mutate(newey_west_se = map_dbl(model, \(x) sqrt(NeweyWest(x)))) %>% 
  unnest(mean) %>% 
  mutate(t_statistic_newey_west = estimate / newey_west_se) %>% 
  select(factor, risk_premium = estimate, t_statistic_newey_west)

left_join(
  price_of_risk,
  price_of_risk_newey_west %>% 
    select(factor, t_statistic_newey_west),
  join_by(factor)
)
```
